info.title: Examance API
info.description:
Privacy-first anonymous exam grading backend.

## Key Security & Architecture Features
- **Zero-Knowledge Encryption**: Student PII, submission scans, and annotations are encrypted client-side (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM) before reaching the server.
- **Multi-factor sign-in**: a session needs a passkey (user verification required) or two distinct factors out of password, passkey and authenticator (TOTP). Fewer than two enrolled means an enrollment-scoped token that reaches nothing else.
- **Recoverable data key**: the client's key is random and wrapped per factor (`key_envelopes`), so a password reset re-wraps it rather than orphaning every vault. The server holds ciphertext only.
- **Session Hygiene**: State stored in HttpOnly cookies (`access_token` 15 min, `refresh_token` 7 days with rotation & reuse detection).
- **Privacy Safeguards**: LaTeX requests redacted in logs (`LaTeXRequest`), IP addresses stored as SHA-256 hashes, k-anonymity (k >= 5) enforced on class stats.
- **LaTeX Engine**: Compilation rendered using sandboxed Tectonic (`tectonic --untrusted`).

post.description: Request a password reset link sent to the user's email address.

schema.title: Response Forgot Password Api V1 Auth Forgot Password Post

post.description:
Ask for an account: mails a verification link to the address; nothing is created until used.

Answers the same whether or not the address already has an account (nothing is mailed then),
and the mail goes out after the response so timing does not tell either.

schema.title: Response Register Api V1 Auth Register Post

post.description:
Verify the address with the mailed token and create the account with the chosen password.

An address on the admin's always-allowed list is approved at once, any other account waits
for an admin (notified). Neither issues a session: the registrant signs in and enrolls then.

What the mailed self-deletion link would delete, for the confirmation page. Deletes nothing:
a mail scanner that opens the link must not delete the account.

GDPR Art. 17: delete the account behind the mailed single-use link (last admin refused).

No session needed (the link proves the mailbox); exercises stay ownerless if the holder asked.
Cookies are left alone (they may belong to another account; this one's tokens die with it).

schema.title: Response Confirm Account Deletion Api V1 Auth Account Deletion Confirm Post

post.description:
Open a password reset with the emailed link (the token is *one* of the two required factors).

Mailbox access alone must not complete a reset. An account that has not finished enrolling has
no second factor to offer, so it gets a `reset_pending` token that completes it alone.

Set the new password and store the re-wrapped data key with it, in one transaction.

A password without its key copy looks like a working account until a sign-in opens nothing.
No envelope: the password wrap is marked unusable and the teacher needs the recovery code.

schema.title: Response Reset Password Api V1 Auth Reset Password Post

post.description:
Change the password of a signed-in account, keeping the session.

The client re-wraps the data key; wrap and password go in one transaction so they never diverge.
The current password uses the `/auth/login` throttle, else this is a cooloff-free oracle.

schema.title: Response Change Password Api V1 Auth Change Password Post

post.description:
Present the password as the *second* factor (`/auth/login` can only open a sign-in).

The account comes from the pending token; taking an email here would make the second step an
account-existence probe. Not reachable in the reset flow (the emailed token stands in).

Present an authenticator code as the second factor.

Second position only: a TOTP code does not identify an account, so accepting it first would
need an email alongside it, a probe for which addresses have accounts.

Spend a backup code in place of the authenticator.

It counts as the ``totp`` factor, so it cannot be paired with a TOTP code to
make up two: it stands in for that factor rather than adding one.

Verify credentials, set httpOnly access + refresh cookies.

Response body contains only { email, role } — never the token value.

Issue new access + refresh cookies, revoke the old refresh token.

Detects concurrent use (token theft) if the token is already revoked.

Clear auth cookies and revoke the refresh token.

Deliberately needs no session, so a teacher with a half-finished or expired sign-in can still
clear their cookies. The revocation is authenticated by the refresh token itself.

Compile LaTeX source to PDF via Tectonic (body limit: BODY_LIMIT_COMPILE).

Extra files come from `resource_exercise_ids` (stored on the server) and `resources` (unsaved
or local-only exercises). LaTeX source is NEVER logged; 422 detail is TeX diagnostics only.

List all exercises in the teacher's exercise library.

schema.title: Response List Exercises Api V1 Exercises Get

post.description: Create a new exercise in the teacher's library.

patch.description: Update group metadata and cascade it to every member variant.

get.description: Get an exercise from the library (own exercises or published ones).

patch.description: Update a library exercise in place.

delete.description:
Delete an exercise from the caller's own library.

Idempotent: always 204, whether or not a row was removed. Only exercises
owned by *teacher* are ever deleted, so a foreign id is a silent no-op —
which also keeps the response from revealing that the id exists.

post.description: Create a new corrected version of an existing exercise (archives previous version).
Create a new parallel variant (e.g. Möbel/Fahrzeug/Wildtier) under the same group.

get.description:
Get count and details of non-deleted exams referencing this exercise.

Only the caller's own exams are reported, so usage of a published exercise
in another teacher's exam is never disclosed.
List an exercise's resource files (metadata only, no bytes).

schema.title: Response List Exercise Resources Api V1 Exercises  Exercise Id  Resources Get

post.description:
Attach a file to an exercise. Uploading an existing filename replaces it.

The filename is sanitised and checked against the bundled LaTeX assets by
the schema; SVG is refused there with a convert-to-PDF hint.

get.description:
Return a resource's raw bytes.

Only png/jpeg/pdf are served under their own media type; anything else is
an opaque download. A stored text/html file returned inline from the API
origin would be stored XSS, so the type is never taken at face value and
sniffing is disabled.

patch.description: Rename a resource file (the LaTeX source must be updated by the caller).

post.description: Upload encrypted student identity ciphertext. Handles upsert for duplicate pseudonym_hmac.

parameters.name: include_scans

schema.description: Include scan_ciphertext_b64/scan_iv_b64 for every submission. Off by default: the scan PDF is the bulk of a submission's payload, so an overview listing all of an exam's submissions must not ship every scan just to show a table. Use has_scan for a presence indicator, and GET /exams/{id}/submissions/{sub_id} to fetch one scan's bytes on demand.

put.description:
Upsert the listed scores; unlisted ones are left alone (clearing is a DELETE).

Rows resolve by (submission_id, exercise_id), never by the client's id, so a
replay updates in place instead of answering 409.

get.description: Accounts, newest first (Admin only). `pending` = waiting for approval.

post.description:
Invite a teacher/admin: create the account without a password (Admin only).

Approved with the given features; the address counts as verified because the mailed
set-password link is the only way in. A pending self-registration for it is superseded.

Approve a pending registration with the given features (Admin only).

Conditional on the account still being pending, so two admins approving at once send one
mail. The registrant's note is erased: it only served this decision.

Reject a pending registration: the account is deleted and the registrant told (Admin only).

Only ever deletes an account that is still pending; an approved one is refused.

patch.description:
Change an account's feature switches (Admin only).

Revoking `server_results` from an account in "all-server" mode does not touch its data: the
next time it opens, the app asks it to move its results into the browser.

delete.description:
Delete an approved account and everything it owns (Admin only).

With `keep_exercises` its library exercises stay ownerless (`services/account_deletion.py`).
Pending registrations go through `/reject`; admins delete their own account in settings.

post.description:
Trigger an admin-forced password reset for an existing user (Admin only).

Emails a single-use reset token; the existing password stays active until the link is used.
For an invited account that never set a password this resends the invitation.

get.description: Domains whose registrations are approved automatically (Admin only).

schema.title: Response List Allowed Domains Api V1 Admin Allowed Domains Get

post.description:
Approve every future registration from a domain automatically (Admin only).

Exact match on the part after '@'; subdomains need their own entry. Existing accounts are
not affected.

patch.description: Change the features future registrations from a domain receive (Admin only).

delete.description: Stop approving a domain automatically (Admin only). Existing accounts stay.

post.description:
Clear a user's authenticator and passkeys (Admin only), the escape hatch for a lost factor.

Does not restore data access: the server cannot read key copies, so the removed factors' wraps
are gone; the recovery code stays the way back (else an admin could read the data).

schema.title: Response Reset User Factors Api V1 Admin Users  User Id  Reset Factors Post

get.description:
Get class statistics for an exam with server-side k≥5 anonymity enforcement.

If count < 5, score details (mean, std_dev) are suppressed to protect privacy.
Get paginated audit logs (Admin only).

schema.title: Response List Audit Logs Api V1 Admin Audit Get

get.description: The account's storage mode (null until chosen) and what it may use.

put.description:
Records the account's storage mode, compare-and-set on `expected`. Moving the results
between server and browser is the client's job and happens before this call; this only
states where they now live.

post.description:
Soft-delete the teacher's student identities and scan submissions (hard delete after 7 days).

LaTeX exercises, exam structures and their resource files stay (teacher-authored content).
A file with personal data (e.g. a pupil photo) must be deleted with the exercise or itself.

schema.title: Response Purge Server Student Data Api V1 User Purge Server Student Data Post

post.description:
Restore soft-deleted student identities and scan submissions for the current teacher
if they are within the 7-day retention grace period.

schema.title: Response Restore Server Data Api V1 User Restore Server Data Post

get.description:
GDPR Art. 15/20: machine-readable copy of the account holder's own data.

Only what the server holds *about the teacher*: account fields, authored exams, audit trail.
Student payloads are excluded (the server cannot read them); use the client-side export.

schema.title: Response Export Own Data Api V1 User Me Export Get

post.description:
GDPR Art. 17: ask to delete one's own account; mails a single-use confirmation link.

The link leads to `POST /auth/account-deletion/confirm` (see `services/account_deletion.py`).
A new request replaces an open one; the last admin account is refused up front.

schema.title: Response Request Account Deletion Api V1 User Me Deletion Request Post

get.description:
Return every wrap for the calling teacher.

Invalidated rows are returned too, marked as such, so the client can tell
"this factor was orphaned by an admin password write" apart from "this
factor was never enrolled" and offer the right recovery path.

put.description:
Replace the teacher's whole envelope set in one transaction.

Wholesale replacement is deliberate. Merging risks leaving a set where the
password wrap is new and the recovery wrap still holds the previous DEK,
which is indistinguishable from a working set until the day someone needs to
recover with it.

delete.description:
Remove a single wrap — used when a passkey is deregistered.

The recovery wrap cannot be deleted this way: it is the factor that always
works, and dropping it would leave the account one forgotten password away
from unreadable data.

get.description:
What this account has enrolled, and whether that is enough to sign in.

Also everything the security page needs to describe each factor: when it was
added, when it last answered, and whether a recovery code is on file. All of
it is about the *authenticated* account — nothing here is reachable before a
factor has been proven, which is what keeps it from being a profile oracle
for an arbitrary email address.

post.description:
Start an authenticator enrollment.

The secret is returned exactly once, inside the `otpauth://` URI. It is not
retrievable afterwards: a teacher who loses the enrollment mid-setup starts
over, which costs a minute, whereas an endpoint that hands back an existing
secret would let anyone holding a session clone the second factor.

Prove the authenticator works, which is what makes it count as a factor.

Returns the backup codes once. They are the way back when the phone is lost,
and they stand in for this factor rather than adding a third.
Replace the backup codes. The previous set stops working immediately.

delete.description:
Remove the authenticator.

Refused when it would drop the account below two sign-in factors, or below
its last means of decrypting its own data. That guard is what makes "any two
of three" safe to offer: without it a teacher could delete their way out of
their own account.

post.description: Options for adding a passkey. Reachable from enrollment as well as a session.

Options for a passkey sign-in.

Unauthenticated and rate-limited: it allocates a challenge per call, and it
takes no account identifier, so there is nothing here to probe with.

Present a passkey as a sign-in factor.

Contributes the `passkey` factor whether it comes first or second. On its
own it satisfies the policy, so a passkey-first sign-in ends in a full
session (or enrollment, for an account with fewer than two factors).

The cookie is read directly rather than through a dependency because this
endpoint has to work both ways: with no session at all (passkey first) and
with a sign-in already part-way through (passkey second).

delete.description:
Remove a passkey.

Refused when it would drop the account below two sign-in factors, or below
its last means of decrypting its own data.

get.description: Whether this deployment accepts training-data donations. Public, read-only.

post.description: Store a batch of teacher-verified checkbox crops, unlinked from the account.

AccountDeletionTokenRequest.title: AccountDeletionTokenRequest
AccountDeletionTokenRequest.description: The token from the mailed self-deletion link. In a body, never a URL, so no log keeps it.

AccountFeatures.title: AccountFeatures
AccountFeatures.description:
The per-account switches an admin sets (app/services/capabilities.py).

server_results: results and student data may live on the server ("all-server").
server_latex: LaTeX may be compiled on the server. Exams and exercises need no switch.

AccountFeaturesUpdate.title: AccountFeaturesUpdate
AccountFeaturesUpdate.description: A partial change of `AccountFeatures`; omitted switches stay as they are.

AccountLogoUpdate.title: AccountLogoUpdate
AccountLogoUpdate.description:
The account's logo choice: ``default`` prints the bundled default logo (MTG), ``none`` prints
no logo, ``custom`` prints ``content_b64``. ``custom`` without content keeps the stored file.
The type is read from the bytes, never from the client.

AdminCreateUserRequest.title: AdminCreateUserRequest
AdminCreateUserRequest.description: An invitation: the account is created approved, the address counts as verified.

ExamLogoUpdate.title: ExamLogoUpdate
ExamLogoUpdate.description:
An exam's logo choice: ``account`` follows the account logo, ``none`` prints no logo,
``custom`` prints ``content_b64``. ``custom`` without content keeps the exam's stored file.

scoring_text.title: Scoring Text
scoring_text.default: Für jedes korrekte Kreuz 1BE; für jedes falsche Kreuz -0,5BE. Pro Teilaufgabe aber immer $\geq$0BE

ExerciseLinkCreate.title: ExerciseLinkCreate
ExerciseLinkCreate.description: Links an existing library exercise to an exam, with optional MC group membership.

ExerciseResourceResponse.title: ExerciseResourceResponse
ExerciseResourceResponse.description: Metadata only — the bytes are fetched from the download endpoint.

KeyEnvelopeIn.title: KeyEnvelopeIn
KeyEnvelopeIn.description: One wrap, as produced in the browser.

KeyEnvelopeSetIn.title: KeyEnvelopeSetIn
KeyEnvelopeSetIn.description:
The complete envelope set for a teacher.

Replacement is wholesale and atomic: a partially written set is a locked-out
teacher, so the endpoint never merges.

LaTeXResource.title: LaTeXResource
LaTeXResource.description:
One file to place next to main.tex for this compilation only.

Nothing here is persisted: the bytes live in the temp working directory and
are removed with it. Teachers in all-local mode keep the only durable copy.
